profile.name: Rynah Tadashi
profile.title: DevOps & Cloud Engineer
profile.intro: I build, automate and secure modern infrastructure to turn complex ideas into reliable solutions.
profile.summary: I hold a bachelor's degree in DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure and am passionate about automation, digitalisation and cybersecurity. Curious and motivated, I want to put my technical skills at the service of the digital transformation of institutions, by contributing to structuring projects with a strong national impact.

education.title: Bachelor's degree — DevOps and cloud infrastructure

experience.summary: Set up an automated and secure deployment infrastructure.
bullets: Automation and deployment: built CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI, dynamic parent/child pipelines) and managed scheduled tasks with Ansible and Crontab for fast, reliable deployments.
Containerisation and production: created and managed Docker and Docker Compose containers for production environments.
Network and security: Traefik, SSL/TLS, hardening of ports and instances to optimise traffic and protect services.
Monitoring and observability: deployed Prometheus, Grafana and Alertmanager for real-time dashboards and monitoring notifications.

projects.name: Automated and secure deployment infrastructure
projects.description: A single push to the main branch provisions the cloud server, builds and publishes the images, scans them, then deploys every application over HTTPS.
projects.application: Three containerised web applications are the workload to deploy: a MERN e-commerce store (React/Vite, Node.js, MongoDB, Redis), a ticketing API and a bus transport application. They were developed by others; I did not write their code.
contribution: AWS infrastructure provisioned with Terraform (VPC, public subnet, internet gateway, security group, EC2 instance), state managed in HCP Terraform
GitLab CI parent/child pipeline: the IP address of the server created by Terraform is passed automatically to the child pipelines
Frontend and backend images built and published to Docker Hub
Image security scanning with Trivy (HIGH and CRITICAL vulnerabilities)
Docker installed on the server by script, then deployment over SSH with Docker Compose
Traefik reverse proxy: routing through Docker labels, HTTP to HTTPS redirection, Let's Encrypt certificates
Monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana and Alertmanager, with email alerts
Server data backed up with an Ansible role
pipeline: build | build images, push Docker Hub

projects.name: Parent/child CI/CD pipeline with GitLab
projects.description: A parent pipeline orchestrates four stages and hands each application over to its own child pipeline.
projects.application: The pipeline ships the three applications of the deployment project (MERN e-commerce, ticketing API, transport application). The application was provided: I did not write its code. My work covers everything around it.
contribution: Parent pipeline in four stages: provision, build, scan, deploy
One child pipeline per application, started with “trigger” and “strategy: depend”
Server IP passed between jobs through a dotenv artifact
Ordering with “needs”: Traefik is deployed before the applications
Credentials (SSH key, Docker Hub, Terraform token) supplied through CI/CD variables
Runs restricted to the main branch
pipeline: deploy | deploy_traefik ▸ child, deploy_bus ▸ child, deploy_ticket ▸ child, deploy_ecommerce ▸ child

projects.name: Containerisation and production behind Traefik
projects.description: Each application runs in its own containers and is exposed over HTTPS only, through a reverse proxy.
projects.application: React/Vite frontend and Node.js backend of the e-commerce store, ticketing API and transport application, each on its own subdomain. The application was provided: I did not write its code. My work covers everything around it.
contribution: Dockerfiles for the frontend and the backend
Images built with Podman in the pipeline, versioned and published to Docker Hub
Trivy scan of the application images and base images (Traefik, MongoDB, Redis)
One Docker Compose file per application, Docker networks shared with Traefik
Traefik 2: label-based routing, HTTP to HTTPS redirection, Let's Encrypt certificates (HTTP challenge)
Script installing Docker and bootstrapping the server

projects.name: Cloud infrastructure with Terraform
projects.description: The server and its network are described as code and created by the pipeline, on AWS and on Google Cloud.
projects.application: The infrastructure hosts the containerised applications of the deployment project. The application was provided: I did not write its code. My work covers everything around it.
contribution: AWS: VPC, public subnet, internet gateway, route table, security group, key pair and EC2 instance
Google Cloud: VPC network, subnet, firewall rules and Compute Engine instance (Ubuntu 22.04)
State and runs managed with HCP Terraform
terraform init, plan and apply run from GitLab CI
Public IP address exposed as an output and reused by the deployment jobs

projects.name: Monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana
projects.description: A full monitoring stack watches the server, the containers and application availability, and alerts by email.
projects.application: Monitoring covers the server, the containers and the HTTP endpoints of the deployed applications. The application was provided: I did not write its code. My work covers everything around it.
contribution: Docker Compose stack: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, Node Exporter, cAdvisor and Blackbox Exporter
Alert rules for system, containers and applications: CPU, memory, disk, container down or restart loop, HTTP errors, response time, SSL certificate expiring soon
Alertmanager: email delivery, message templates, routing by severity and inhibition rules
Blackbox HTTP probes on the applications
Grafana data source and dashboards provisioned from files
Interfaces exposed over HTTPS behind Traefik

projects.name: Backup automation with Ansible
projects.description: A playbook pulls the production server's data back to a backup machine.
projects.application: The backed-up data belongs to the applications deployed on the cloud server. The application was provided: I did not write its code. My work covers everything around it.
contribution: Ansible playbook and “backup” role, server inventory
rsync installed on the remote server
Pull-mode synchronisation to the backup machine
Exclusions: Git repositories, logs, temporary files, node_modules
Scheduled execution with Crontab
